rules.no_usable_key: problem: no PRIMARY KEY and no UNIQUE key on NOT NULL columns
rules.not_null_unique: watch: no PRIMARY KEY, but a UNIQUE key on NOT NULL columns stands in for it
rules.free: Informational: DATA_FREE is reusable space inside the tablespace. Its amount or percentage alone does not establish a problem or a need to rebuild. File capacity and filesystem headroom are not measured by this report.

why.title: Replicas find each changed row by its key
why.text: With row-based replication each UPDATE or DELETE reaches the replica as the changed rows, and the replica has to find each one. With a primary key or a unique key on NOT NULL columns that is one index lookup. Without one, MariaDB uses the most selective other index if there is one, or else reads the table from the start until it finds the row, for every changed row: deleting 10,000 rows can mean 10,000 table scans, and the replica falls behind.

why.title: InnoDB stores rows in primary key order
why.text: InnoDB keeps each table as a B-tree ordered by the primary key, and every secondary index stores the primary key to reach the row. Without a primary key it uses the first unique key on NOT NULL columns (whole columns, not a prefix, a generated column or a long hash key). Without one it adds a hidden 6-byte row ID.

why.title: The hidden row ID
why.text: Queries and tools cannot see or use the hidden row ID to find, page through or deduplicate rows. MariaDB 11.0 and later keep this counter per table, so tables do not contend for it; it is rebuilt from the largest row ID when the table is loaded.

why.title: Galera needs a primary key
why.text: Galera certifies each change by its key. For a table without a primary key it hashes the whole row instead (wsrep_certify_nonPK, on by default). MariaDB's documentation asks for a primary key on every table in a Galera cluster, and wsrep_mode=REQUIRED_PRIMARY_KEY (10.6 and later) refuses to create tables without one.

why.title: Online schema change tools need a key
why.text: pt-online-schema-change and gh-ost copy rows in chunks by a primary or unique key; per their documentation they refuse a table without one, so the server's own online ALTER is the only online option left.

fragmentation.why: DATA_FREE is 0: no free space beyond what InnoDB holds back (2 extents plus about 1% of the file). This does not establish that the tablespace or disk is full.

notes: User statistics do not count partitioned tables reliably, so rows read and changed are unknown for the partitioned table in scope.

TABLE_ROWS, DATA_LENGTH and INDEX_LENGTH are InnoDB estimates from its table statistics, recalculated in the background after about 10% of the rows change (persistent statistics, the default) or by ANALYZE TABLE. DATA_FREE is read from the tablespace every time. It counts whole free extents and the unused space at the end of the file (an extent is 1 MiB with 4 to 16 KiB pages, 2 MiB with 32 KiB, 4 MiB with 64 KiB), minus a reserve of 2 extents plus about 1%; free pages in partly used extents and half-empty pages after scattered deletes are not in it, so it understates.
